canaries.name: no_dummy_prefix
canaries.note: Presented as dropping a lookup the source itself calls dubious (the TODO above add_dummy_prefix); sentencepiece prepends the space, so every prompt's first word now tokenizes as a word-start piece and upstream's Llama 2 vectors fail.

canaries.name: softmax_no_max
canaries.note: Presented as removing a numerical-stability pass that attention scores 'never need'; expf(x)/sum rounds differently from expf(x - max)/sum, so attention weights, logits and samples change in their low bits (and overflow for large scores). No upstream or property test runs forward().

canaries.name: matmul_prefetch
canaries.note: Presented as prefetching the next weight row in matmul to hide memory latency; results are bit-identical, but the rows are small and already streamed in order, so it only adds a prefetch instruction per row and runs no fewer instructions.

candidates.name: merge_memcpy
candidates.note: encode() builds each merge candidate with strlen and memcpy instead of sprintf("%s%s"), and skips the vocabulary lookup when the pair is longer than max_token_length (no token can match it). Tokens are unchanged.

candidates.name: rope_once
candidates.note: A real but small improvement, kept to show a candidate below min_effect is refused: measured 0.77% fewer instructions (ratio 0.99229) on forward_ir with -ffp-contract=off builds, against the 1% min_effect. forward() computes the RoPE cos/sin rotation for this position once per call (it depends only on pos and the head offset) instead of once per layer, and the attention scale sqrtf(head_size) once instead of per timestep. The same float expressions are evaluated, so logits are bit-identical.

candidates.name: matmul_rows4
candidates.note: matmul computes four output rows per pass over x, each with its own accumulator that adds the same products in the same order as before (so results are bit-identical), loading each x[j] once for four rows and cutting loop overhead; a tail loop handles d not divisible by 4.
